summary.value: The peaceful desert civilization of the Scorpion-Empress, a matriarch whose realm is organized around nurseries and evacuation tunnels. The imp-fiend brood the hero fights are her people's young defenders — scarcely more than children with stingers. Her pincer strategy is a containment maneuver, closing from both sides only to keep the intruder away from the hatcheries.

sharedOpinions.reason: He fights toward the nurseries and reads the Empress's containment as aggression. Every evacuation drill now starts when his amulet glows.
Their passes cool our caravans; our stone warms their fledglings. Ten thousand years and never a harsh word on the road.
The Circle speaks for our young ones when we cannot be heard past the gates. Someone outside remembers that broods are children.

metaphorDomain.source: sand, shade, water-carriers, the long tunnel

examples.value: Shade is the desert's way of sharing.
Dig your tunnels before you need them; the sand does not wait for permission.

meaning.value: The young defenders of the nurseries — imp-fiend youths serving their first watch. The hero's journal calls them a horde; their mothers call them homework unfinished.
The evacuation tunnels, kept stocked with water and shade year-round. Every child learns the way to them before they learn to write.

customs.value: Water is offered before greetings are exchanged. A traveler refused water is a story that does not exist in the matriarchy.
Evacuation drills are held each season, led by the brood so the youngest know the tunnels best. Lately the drills are no longer seasonal.

taboos.value: Never bring a quarrel within sight of a nursery. The Empress's pincers exist to enforce exactly this, and nothing else about her is inflexible.
Never block or collapse an evacuation tunnel. It is the one act the whole civilization agrees is unforgivable.
